For an English guy, this is heaven. We adore Indian food.
Nov 2025 • Couples
As an English guy visiting Ho Chi Minh City, I had absolutely no idea what to expect from the Dahi Handi festival — but what an experience! The energy, the noise, the colour — it’s something you just don’t get back home.

I stumbled across the event by chance, drawn in by the music and laughter echoing through the streets. What really amazed me was the sheer enthusiasm of everyone involved — whole families, from toddlers to grandparents, were out cheering and dancing. Then came the main event: the human pyramid! I’d seen photos before, but seeing it live was unbelievable. The teamwork and trust between the climbers were incredible — all to reach and smash that little pot of curd high above the crowd.

There was this beautiful sense of unity — locals and visitors all clapping and shouting encouragement. It felt festive but also deeply meaningful, celebrating teamwork, tradition, and a shared joy that crossed every boundary.

I have to give credit to the organisers too. Everything felt well-run and safe, and even with the huge crowds, there was an atmosphere of warmth and welcome. I was handed a bit of prasad (sweet curd) afterwards and honestly, that small gesture summed it up — pure hospitality.

If you ever find yourself in Ho Chi Minh City when Dahi Handi is on, don’t miss it. It’s noisy, chaotic, heart-pounding — and absolutely brilliant. One of those travel moments that sticks with you long after you’ve left.
